label: Divrei HaYamim Aleph (1 Chronicles) — Part 2 — Chapters 10–29
summary_plain: Divrei HaYamim Aleph chapters 10 through 29 retell Dawid's reign from the death of Sha'ul to Dawid's final charge to Shelomoh. Dawid captures Yerushalayim and brings the Ark of the Covenant into the city with singing and dancing. He desires to build a house for YHWH, but YHWH says: Your son will build the house — I will establish his throne forever. Dawid prepares the materials for the temple, organizes the Levitical musicians and gatekeepers, and charges Shelomoh: Be strong and courageous. Know the Creator of your father and serve him with a whole heart.
summary_scholarly: The ACR reads from DSS fragments (4QChr) and the Orit Ge'ez. The Chronicler retells Dawid's reign with a distinctive emphasis: the military and political failures recorded in Shemu'el (Bat-Sheva, Amnon, Avshalom's revolt) are largely omitted. The Chronicler focuses on Dawid's role as temple preparer, worship organizer, and covenant transmitter. This is not historical falsification — it is theological selection. The Chronicler writes for the post-exilic community that needs to know its liturgical and institutional origins. Dawid's organization of the Levitical musicians (chapters 25-26) establishes the worship infrastructure that produced the Tehillim. The Chronicler's Dawid is the singer, the worshipper, the one who prepared everything so that YHWH's house could be built. The covenant promise in chapter 17 parallels 2 Shemu'el 7 — YHWH's unconditional oath to Dawid's line.

key_terms.definition: David's first attempt to bring the Ark failed when Uzza was struck dead; the second attempt succeeded with proper Levitical carrying procedures
Uzza reached out to steady the Ark when the oxen stumbled; YHWH's anger burned against him and he died — the Ark must be carried only by Levites using poles, not placed on a cart
When the Ark is installed in the tent David pitched for it, he leads a psalm combining portions of Tehillim 96, 105, and 106 — a liturgical moment of covenant worship
YHWH's promise to build David a house/dynasty — 'I will raise up your offspring after you and establish his kingdom'; David cannot build the Temple but his son will
YHWH tells David through the prophet Natan: 'You shall not build me a house to dwell in' — David is a man of war; his son will build the Temple in a time of rest

The Adversary (satan — the accuser role) incites David to count Yisra'el; YHWH is angered; David chooses three days of plague; 70,000 die; the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusite becomes the Temple site

In Shemu'el Bet 24:1 it is YHWH who incites David; in Divrei HaYamim 21:1 it is the Adversary — an adversarial figure in YHWH's council carrying out a function. This is documented as a textual variant, not a theological contradiction

David gathers materials (cedar, iron, bronze, gold, silver), organizes the Levites, and commissions Shlomo to build the Temple — the most extensive preparation for YHWH's house in the Hebrew scriptures
David organizes the Levites by age and function: 24 divisions of priests, singers, gatekeepers, and treasury officials — a priestly system designed for the permanent Temple

David's prayer: 'All things come from you, and of your own have we given you' — a declaration that the resources gathered for the Temple belong to YHWH and are returned to him, not donated by human initiative

faq.question: Why was the first attempt to bring the Ark to Yerushalayim a failure?
faq.answer: David placed the Ark on a new cart — a Plishtim method — instead of having the Levites carry it on poles as YHWH commanded. When Uzza reached out to steady it, YHWH's anger burned and Uzza died. The proper method required Levites carrying it on their shoulders.

faq.question: What is the significance of David's psalm in ch.16?
faq.answer: It combines portions of Tehillim 96, 105, and 106 — showing that the Psalter was understood as a living covenant liturgy, used at key moments of worship. The psalm's themes are YHWH's glory among the nations, his covenant with Avraham, and national praise.

faq.question: What does YHWH promise David in the Davidic covenant of ch.17?
faq.answer: YHWH promises to establish David's dynasty forever: a son from his own body will build the Temple, YHWH will be a father to that son, and his throne will be established forever. David cannot build the Temple because he is a man of war.

faq.question: Why does the census anger YHWH?
faq.answer: Divrei HaYamim states the Adversary incited David to count Yisra'el. The census represents a trust in human military numbers rather than in YHWH as Yisra'el's true defender — it is a failure of covenant faith expressed as a political act.

faq.question: What is the significance of Ornan's threshing floor?
faq.answer: David purchases it to build an altar after YHWH stops the plague there. YHWH answers by fire from heaven on the altar — this site becomes the place where Shlomo will later build the Temple. The Temple of YHWH is built on the spot where judgment was turned back.

faq.question: Why does David prepare materials for the Temple if he cannot build it?
faq.answer: David's love for YHWH means he prepares everything his son will need — gold, silver, bronze, iron, timber, and stone in enormous quantities. His preparation is an act of covenant devotion even though the honor of building goes to Shlomo.

faq.question: How does David organize the Levites in chs 23-26?
faq.answer: He divides them into 24 priestly divisions (the sons of Aharon), organizes the singers under Asaf, Heman, and Yedutun, establishes gatekeeping divisions, and appoints treasury officials — a complete administrative structure for permanent Temple service.

faq.question: What does David's prayer in ch.29 reveal about his theology?
faq.answer: David declares that everything given for the Temple came first from YHWH — the people are returning to YHWH what was already his. He acknowledges Yisra'el as foreigners and sojourners before YHWH, as all their ancestors were.

faq.question: What is the textual significance of the census being incited by 'an adversary' in Divrei HaYamim vs. YHWH in Shemu'el?
faq.answer: This is a documented textual variant between the two accounts. In Shemu'el Bet 24:1 YHWH incites David; in Divrei HaYamim 21:1 an adversarial figure does so. The variant reflects the developing role of the adversary figure in the divine council across the Hebrew scriptural tradition — both are pre-corruption primary texts.

faq.question: What charge does David give Shlomo about building the Temple?
faq.answer: Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or dismayed. YHWH is with you and will not leave you until all the Temple work is finished. Seek YHWH with a whole heart and willing mind — YHWH searches all hearts and understands every thought.
